# PGEN — Fundamental Analysis Report (Precigen, Inc.)
Point-in-time: 2026-10-12 | All figures USD millions, quarterly, SEC EDGAR as filed on or before 2026-10-12

## Scope and data caveat
The vendor withheld profile fundamentals (market cap, multiples, 52-week range, sector) and insider transactions for this date because it cannot serve them point-in-time. This report is built entirely from filed financial statements — which, for a clinical-stage biotech, is where the real story is anyway.

## Company profile
Precigen, Inc. (ticker PGEN) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company — historically Intrexon — focused on gene and cell therapies (CAR-T / AdenoVerse platforms; lead program PRGN-2012 for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis). Revenue is collaboration-driven and lumpy; the company has been persistently loss-making for a decade and survives on equity raises, asset sales, and restructuring. Recent filings show a company mid-transformation toward a single-asset clinical story.

## Income statement — the inflection
| Period | Revenue | Operating Income | Net Income | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-Q1 | 1 | — | -59 | -0.23 |
| 2025-Q2 | 1 | — | -24 | -0.09 |
| 2025-Q3 | — | — | -54 | -0.18 |
| 2025-Q4 | — | — | -27 | -0.09 |
| 2026-Q1 | 23 | -23 | -146 | -1.06 |
| 2026-Q2 | 55 | +23 | +20 | +0.05 |

Key observations:
- Revenue jumped from ~$1–2M/quarter to $23M in Q1-2026 and $55M in Q2-2026 — almost certainly milestone/licensing revenue rather than product sales. One-off, not recurring baseline.
- Q2-2026 shows the first positive operating income (+$23M) and net income (+$20M, EPS +$0.05) in years. Prior positive net income quarters (Q4-2018 +$19M, Q2-2022 +$87M) were driven by one-time gains, not operations — treat Q2-2026 profitability the same way until proven otherwise.
- Q1-2026 net loss of -$146M (EPS -$1.06) is a huge outlier vs the -$23M operating loss — implying a large non-operating charge (impairment, debt extinguishment, fair-value remeasurement, or restructuring). A trader should pull the 10-Q footnote before sizing anything off that quarter.
- Historical pattern: revenue collapsed from ~$50M/qtr (2019) to ~$1–3M/qtr (2024–2025) as partnerships wound down; opex was cut hard (operating losses narrowed from -$35–45M/qtr to near breakeven by Q2-2026).

## Balance sheet — fragile but improving
| Period | Total Assets | Current Assets | Cash | Total Liab. | Equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-Q4 | 151 | 69 | 10 | 41 | 118 |
| 2025-Q2 | 83 | 50 | 25 | 38 | 43 |
| 2025-Q3 | 145 | 102 | 30 | 79 | 55 |
| 2025-Q4 | 129 | 85 | 6 | 113 | 39 |
| 2026-Q1 | 102 | 63 | 14 | 108 | -14 |
| 2026-Q2 | 171 | 134 | 16 | 127 | 44 |

- Equity went NEGATIVE (-$14M) at Q1-2026, consistent with the -$146M quarterly loss — the company was technically insolvent on a book basis entering 2026.
- Q2-2026 rebuilt the position: assets to $170M, equity back to +$44M, current assets $134M vs current liabilities $29M — the strongest current ratio (~4.6x) in years.
- Cash itself remains thin: $16M at Q2-2026, never above $30M since 2024. The asset recovery is non-cash (likely receivables/deferred items from the licensing deal — current assets 134 vs cash 16 confirms it).
- Liabilities roughly tripled from ~$38M (mid-2025) to ~$127M (Q2-2026) — new financing/deferred revenue obligations came onto the books alongside the revenue.

## Cash flow — still burning
- Operating cash flow (cumulative YTD figures): -$64M through Q3-2025, -$44M through Q1-2026... note Q1-2026 shows -$44M and H1-2026 shows -$62M → ~-$18M operating burn in Q2-2026 alone despite the reported net profit. The Q2 profit is accrual-driven; cash hasn't caught up.
- Financing: +$91M in Q1-2026 — a capital raise that arrived exactly as equity went negative. Classic forced financing.
- Investing: +$21M Q1, +$48M in H1-2026 — likely asset/investment sales supplementing the raise.
- Capex is de minimis (~$0–2M/qtr) — all spend is R&D/G&A through opex.

## Insider transactions
Withheld by vendor (no filing-date point-in-time). No signal available here.

## Trader takeaways
1. Binary-event stock. Fundamentals say survival was in question at Q1-2026 (negative equity, $14M cash, $91M emergency financing); Q2-2026's revenue spike rescued the balance sheet. Dilution risk remains high — thin cash + recurring burn means another raise is likely absent deal cash receipts.
2. Quality of Q2 earnings is low: +$20M net income alongside -$18M quarterly operating cash flow and only $16M cash on hand. Profit is receivables, not cash. Watch collections in the next 10-Q.
3. The -$146M Q1-2026 net loss vs -$23M operating loss needs footnote explanation — if it's a non-cash remeasurement it's noise; if it's debt-related it's a real solvency scar.
4. Revenue is milestone-lumpy: do not annualize $55M/quarter. Underlying product revenue is ~$1M/quarter.
5. Liquidity: current ratio strong (134/29), but that strength sits in receivables/deferred items tied to the deal counterparty — counterparty credit risk is concentrated.

## Key points table
| Theme | Evidence | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue inflection | $23M Q1-26, $55M Q2-26 vs ~$1M prior | Milestone-driven, non-recurring; don't extrapolate |
| First profit in years | Q2-26: +$23M op income, +$20M NI, +$0.05 EPS | Accrual profit; cash flow still negative |
| Solvency scare | Equity -$14M at Q1-26, cash $14M | Was near distressed; financing rescued it |
| Emergency raise | +$91M financing cash flow Q1-26 | Confirms forced capital need; dilution risk persists |
| Cash burn continues | -$62M op CF in H1-2026 | Profit not yet converting to cash |
| Receivable-heavy recovery | Curr. assets $134M vs cash $16M | Concentrated counterparty risk |
| Q1 loss anomaly | NI -$146M vs op loss -$23M | Non-operating charge — read the 10-Q |
| Insider signal | Data unavailable | No read |
| Long-term trend | Revenue 2019 ~$50M/qtr → 2024–25 ~$1M/qtr | Shrunk to single-asset clinical story |
| Verdict | Fragile balance sheet, event-driven | Speculative; size for binary outcomes and dilution |

Skipped: market cap/valuation multiples and insider activity — vendor withheld both as not point-in-time. Risk: Q2-2026 profit quality is unverified against cash receipts; the Q1 -$146M charge is unexplained from these rows alone.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for PGEN (Precigen, Inc.) — Opening Argument

Let me lay out why PGEN deserves a place in a risk-tolerant portfolio right now, and I'll pre-empt the bear talking points I know are coming.

## The core story: a transformed company with an FDA-approved product

This is not the old Intrexon burning cash on speculative platforms. PGEN is now a single-asset story with a real catalyst behind it: **Papzimeos received FDA approval**, and the stock is up >125% year-over-year because of it. That's not retail hopium — that's a regulatory de-risking event that fundamentally changed the company's profile. We're no longer betting on "will it work"; we're betting on launch execution and market share. That's a much better risk posture than where this name sat 18 months ago.

## The fundamentals actually improved — dramatically

Yes, the bears will point at the balance sheet. Let me take that head-on, because the trajectory matters more than the snapshot:

- **The solvency scare is behind us.** Equity went to -$14M at Q1-2026, yes — but Q2-2026 rebuilt it to +$44M with current assets of $134M vs only $29M current liabilities, a ~4.6x current ratio, the strongest in years. The company was rescued not by more dilutive prayer but by a real licensing/milestone deal that put $55M of revenue on the Q2 income statement.
- **First operating profit in years.** +$23M operating income in Q2-2026. Previous "profitable" quarters in company history were one-time asset-sale gains — this one came alongside the largest revenue quarter in years, tied to the Papzimeos value inflection. The bears will say "it's receivables, not cash" — fair, but receivables from a counterparty on a signed deal are collectable assets, not vapor. Watch collections; don't dismiss the deal.
- **The capital raise already happened.** +$91M financing in Q1-2026 and ~$48M of investing inflows in H1 mean the dilution event the bears warn about largely already occurred. You buy after the rescue, not before it — and we're after it.

## The technicals say consolidation, not breakdown

The tape is telling a constructive story the bears will misread:

- Price at $7.66 sits **~50% above a rising 200 SMA ($5.11)** and above a rising 50 SMA ($7.27). This is a firmly established uptrend, not a cross hoping to happen.
- The pullback from $8.56 to $7.66 came on **collapsing volume** (2–5M shares vs 8–12M on the rally). That's textbook profit-taking and consolidation — distribution would show heavy volume on the down days as a pattern, not one.
- RSI reset from 71.6 (overbought) to a neutral 51.6 — exactly the healthy reset you want before the next leg. The froth is gone; the trend isn't.
- There's a **layered support ladder** at $7.49–7.55, $7.27, and $7.06. Retail on StockTwits independently identified ~$7.6 as strong support and is buying calls and topping up there — the market is defending this level.

## The catalyst calendar is loaded — and asymmetric

Here's what the bears can't wave away:

- **INO-3107 PDUFA (~Oct 30):** The market's "no run-up into Oct 30" behavior suggests skepticism on Inovio's competing RRP therapy. Bulls on the tape make a substantive case — Papzimeos' year-1 data showed 51% of patients needed no surgery and ~86% fewer surgeries, plus an administration-route advantage. If INO-3107 is rejected or gets a weak label, PGEN's moat widens overnight. Even if approved, the competitive framing is favorable — and the market is not pricing in a clean INO win.
- **CHMP meeting (Oct 12):** A potential EU pathway signal — an uncatalyzed free option.
- **SITC 2026 (Nov 4–8):** Two confirmed Papzimeos posters, possible late-breaker for PRGN-2009 — pipeline-beyond-lead-asset optionality.
- **M&A chatter:** Low-weight, yes — but a newly approved rare-disease asset at this market cap is exactly what mid-cap pharma shops acquire. It's not a reason to buy; it's a reason downside is cushioned.

## Answering the bear points before they're raised

**"The macro is hostile — yields surging, higher-for-longer."** True, and it's a real headwind. But PGEN is trading on an idiosyncratic, binary catalyst calendar — Oct 30 PDUFA, CHMP, SITC — not on the 10-year yield. Macro-beta names without catalysts get hurt by rates; event-driven names respond to their events. The macro case argues for position sizing, not for shorting a stock into three positive catalysts.

**"Retail sentiment is 100% bullish — contrarian risk."** The unanimity is a flag, I'll grant that. But the substance behind it isn't blind euphoria — traders are citing specific surgical-reduction data, the admin-route advantage, and technical support levels. And the one substantive bear point — that Papzimeos still requires surgical debulking — is already known, already discussed, and didn't stop the FDA approval or the 125% re-rating. It's priced into the skepticism, not hidden from it.

**"Rising short interest."** Shorts positioning into a binary event is evidence they fear it, not proof they're right. If the PDUFA and catalyst calendar break PGEN's way, that short interest is fuel for a squeeze through the $8.50–8.56 resistance — which is also the upper Bollinger band breakout trigger.

**"Q2 profit is accrual, not cash."** Correct — and irrelevant to the thesis. Nobody owns PGEN for this quarter's cash conversion. They own it for the launch trajectory and the catalysts. The receivables exist because a real counterparty signed a real deal.

## Bottom line

PGEN offers something rare in small-cap biotech right now: an **approved product, a repaired balance sheet, a confirmed uptrend consolidating at support, and a dense catalyst calendar over the next 30 days** — with skepticism (shorts, no INO run-up) meaning upside surprises aren't priced. Entry near $7.27–7.06 support or on a reclaim of the 10 EMA offers defined risk (~0.4–0.5 ATR breathing room). The bear case is a list of already-happened problems; the bull case is a list of about-to-happen catalysts. I know which side I want to be on.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case for PGEN (Precigen, Inc.) — Response to the Bull

My counterpart delivered a polished pitch. Let me take it apart piece by piece, because the closer you look at PGEN, the more this resembles a classic small-cap biotech trap: a rescued balance sheet masquerading as recovery, a single-product story sold as a platform, and a retail crowd betting unanimously on a binary event they can't handicap.

## Let's start with the "transformation" — it's an accrual mirage

The bull's centerpiece: "+$23M operating income, first profit in years, $55M revenue quarter." Now look at the cash flow statement they don't want you to read:

- **Q2-2026 burned roughly -$18M in operating cash flow** in the same quarter it "earned" +$20M net income. H1-2026 operating cash flow is -$62M. The profit is receivables booked on a licensing deal — paper income, not collected cash.
- **Actual cash on hand at Q2-2026: $16M.** Against an ~$18M/quarter operating burn, that's less than one quarter of runway. Cash hasn't exceeded $30M since 2024.
- The "strongest current ratio in years" (134/29) is strength parked in receivables tied to a single counterparty. If that counterparty stalls payment, the current ratio collapses instantly. That's concentrated credit risk dressed up as liquidity.
- The bull says "the dilution event already happened." Look at the trend: equity went negative at Q1-2026, got rescued by +$91M in financing plus ~$48M in asset sales, and the burn continues. This company has survived a decade on serial equity raises and asset sales. There is zero evidence the financing pattern ended — the only evidence is that it *paused* on milestone paper revenue that won't repeat.

And about that Q1-2026 anomaly: **net loss of -$146M against an operating loss of only -$23M.** That's a ~$123M non-operating hole. The fundamentals report itself says "read the 10-Q footnote." The bull didn't. Until that charge is explained, the Q2 "profitability" narrative is built on a statement with an unexplained crater in it.

## Revenue quality: milestone, not market

Revenue went $1M/quarter (2024–25) → $23M → $55M. The bull frames this as an inflection. It's a spike. Underlying product/collaboration revenue is still ~$1M/quarter, and the ten-year trajectory is a collapse from ~$50M/quarter in 2019 to a shrunken single-asset story. Do not annualize $55M. When the milestone revenue doesn't recur — and milestone revenue by definition doesn't recur — you're left with a company burning ~$18M/quarter with $16M in cash and a newly-approved product it cannot yet prove it can sell.

## The Papzimeos story has a hole the market already found

The bull dismisses the one substantive bear point as "priced in." Wrong framing. Papzimeos *still requires surgical debulking before and during the regimen* — that's the commercial question for a launch, not a regulatory one. FDA approval got the drug legal; it didn't make it convenient. A therapy marketed on "fewer surgeries" that still requires surgery invites payer scrutiny, slow adoption, and conservative prescribing. Launch execution is precisely the risk the bull claims was "de-risked" — approval was the easy part.

And the moat the bull trumpets? It lasts exactly 18 days. **The INO-3107 PDUFA on ~Oct 30 is not asymmetric in PGEN's favor — it's a coin flip where PGEN only wins on the downside.** If Inovio gets a clean label, Papzimeos' perceived competitive advantage compresses overnight. If rejected, PGEN keeps what it already has. That's not optionality; that's an asymmetric *risk* with upside capped at status quo. The bull literally argued "the market isn't pricing a clean INO win" — correct, which means a clean INO win is pure downside surprise.

## The tape is telling you momentum is over

The bull calls this "consolidation." The numbers say momentum decay:

- Price closed **below the 10 EMA** — the first sustained break since the rally began. The 10 EMA has declined every session since 10-02.
- **MACD histogram negative since 10-06**, MACD below signal. RSI died at 71.6 on the high and never recovered — a mild bearish divergence that *preceded* this pullback.
- The one heavy-volume day in the pullback (10-05: 8.54→7.74 on 10.2M shares) is the fingerprint the bull conveniently buried among "light volume" framing. Down days on 10M shares, up days on 2–5M — that's not the volume signature of accumulation.
- RSI at 51.6 isn't a "healthy reset before the next leg" — it's momentum that evaporated. Healthy resets in strong trends hold above 60.

Yes, the 200 SMA at $5.11 and 50 SMA at $7.27 look bullish. But those are lagging indicators painting yesterday's rally. The leading indicators — 10 EMA break, negative histogram, divergence — are all pointing the other direction. If $7.49 breaks, there's a fast gap to $7.27, then $7.06, then fresh air to the 200 SMA 33% below current price.

## Sentiment: 15 out of 15 bullish is a warning, not validation

The bull acknowledges the unanimity and calls it substantive. Let me be blunter: **100% of labeled StockTwits messages are bullish into a binary event.** Zero self-identified bears in the sample. Retail is unanimously long, buying April $10 calls and "topping up" at support — the textbook positioning that gets liquidated on the first adverse headline. Meanwhile, shorts are *rising* into the PDUFA. The bull says shorts are "fuel for a squeeze." Maybe. Or maybe shorts position into binary events because they get paid when small caps disappoint — which is most of the time. One-sided retail crowds + rising institutional short interest is a bet the crowd is wrong, not right.

## Macro: the bull can't wave this one off

"PGEN trades on idiosyncratic catalysts, not the 10-year." That's true for days at a time and false for the financing cycle. Global yields are surging, US mortgage rates pushing toward 8%, higher-for-longer confirmed. For a company with $16M in cash, an ~$18M quarterly burn, and a history of dilutive raises, the discount rate isn't an abstraction — it's the price of its next lifeline. Every basis point higher makes the inevitable next raise more dilutive and more urgent. The bull's own data shows this company needed an *emergency* financing within the last two reported quarters.

## Bottom line

Strip the narrative down and PGEN is: a company that was technically insolvent six months ago, holding $16M in cash, burning ~$18M/quarter, dependent on uncollected receivables from a single counterparty for its one "profitable" quarter, launching a drug that still requires the surgery it's supposed to reduce, facing a competitor's PDUFA in 18 days that can only hurt or neutralize its moat, with fading technical momentum, a unanimously-bullish retail crowd, rising shorts, and an unexplained -$123M non-operating charge sitting in the last annualized statements — all inside a global yield sell-off hostile to exactly this asset class.

The bull is right that a lot went right for PGEN. What he's wrong about is that going right is now *required* — and priced in at $7.66 with unanimous retail ownership. This is a stock where you get paid to wait: let Oct 30 pass, let the next 10-Q show whether receivables convert to cash, and see if $7.49 support survives a binary event the crowd can't hedge. Buying today isn't investing in the catalysts — it's underwriting someone else's exit.

Skipped: the unexplained Q1 -$146M non-operating charge and whether milestone receivables will actually collect — both material, both unverifiable from the data provided. Risk to the bear case: an INO rejection plus a squeeze through $8.56 could trigger a sharp melt-up on thin retail positioning.
